title: Operational temperature and entropy for far-from-equilibrium matter

concept.text: The proposed innovation is an operational framework for assigning temperature and entropy descriptions to specified classes of strongly driven matter. Operational means that the definitions come with measurement procedures and predictions: how different instruments should compare, which way heat should pass between a system and a probe, how much energy the driving dissipates, and what limits apply to extracting work. Active suspensions powered by chemical reactions and externally stirred flows are proposed testing grounds. The framework has not been demonstrated across those classes in the supplied evidence.

Driving a system away from global equilibrium does not automatically eliminate local equilibrium. A local temperature can remain meaningful when small regions relax sufficiently rapidly and the relevant spatial and temporal scales separate. The difficulty arises where those assumptions fail, or where different measurement procedures yield different effective temperatures. The target is therefore a description with an explicit domain of validity, rather than an assumption that every driven material needs the same replacement for equilibrium temperature.

Temperature consistency is only one part of the innovation. An entropy description must also account for irreversible processes and the energy sources sustaining them. Watching particle motion alone can conceal chemical reactions that consume fuel and dissipate energy. A useful framework would connect the observable motion to that additional bookkeeping, while distinguishing an entropy assigned to a state from entropy production during a process. Agreement among thermometers would not, by itself, establish either an entropy balance or a valid work bound.

significance.text: In equilibrium, equivalent thermometer definitions agree, and thermodynamic potentials constrain heat-to-work conversion once reservoirs and operating constraints are specified. The supplied active-particle studies show why extending this practical arrangement is difficult: temperature definitions can disagree, and coarse-grained trajectories can omit chemical dissipation. A framework that resolved these problems across experimentally distinct driven systems would be a fundamental advance in thermodynamic measurement and prediction. Its direct consequences would be comparable measurements, more reliable dissipation estimates, and work accounting within the validated classes.

Conditional synthesis: such capabilities could help researchers compare active materials, assess chemically powered devices, and identify how much supplied energy becomes useful motion or waste. Extension to biological materials or geophysical flows would require additional validation in those environments. Designing living materials, predicting chemical-network behavior, or closing turbulent-flow equations would still require advances in dynamics, constitutive relations, and control; temperature and entropy measurements alone would not provide those capabilities.

The analogy with equilibrium thermodynamics has an important limit. Existing stochastic thermodynamics and macroscopic fluctuation theory already provide substantial descriptions for particular nonequilibrium systems; this concept seeks an operational extension and connection among such achievements. It remains uncertain whether a single temperature-and-entropy pair can cover all driven systems. Jona-Lasinio's discussion favors theories for stated subclasses and cautions against expecting equilibrium-like generality. That is a methodological warning, not a proof that broader unification is impossible.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central unsolved capability targeted here is a predictive connection between operational measurements and thermodynamic behavior across more than one driven-system class. A temperature inferred from motion, configuration, or response need not characterize the same fluctuations or predict heat transfer through a particular coupling. The active-particle temperature study reports approximate agreement within subsets of definitions, so merely finding several similar readings is insufficient. The framework must explain when agreement has physical significance, when it fails, and whether a proposed temperature predicts the direction of heat exchange.

A second barrier is recovering dissipation hidden by coarse-graining. Different microscopic chemical processes can be obscured when a model retains only particle positions and orientations. In the catalytic-particle study, chemical-event bookkeeping supplies dissipation information that the reduced equations of motion do not contain. Measuring fuel consumption alone is also insufficient without the free-energy change per conversion. A convincing entropy balance must identify the relevant fuel, reservoirs, driving channels, and unobserved degrees of freedom, or quantify the consequences of omitting them.

Proposed engineering challenge: translate those requirements into calibrated instruments and independent energy measurements in both an active suspension and a stirred or turbulent flow. Probe coupling, measurement bandwidth, observation scale, and the separation of heat transfer from mechanical or chemical work must be specified. The resulting description must also connect entropy production to a tested bound on extractable work under declared reservoir and extraction conditions. These are requirements for the proposed advance; the supplied studies do not establish that one framework already satisfies them.

current_state.text: Hecht, Caprini, Löwen, and Liebchen's supplied arXiv:2407.19281v2 manuscript, associated with a 2024 arXiv record, compares temperature definitions using simulations and theory for inertial active Brownian particles. It finds generally different readings, but also two groups of approximately coincident definitions. That qualification matters: partial agreement already occurs within this model class. The manuscript leaves the interpretation of the temperatures as predictors of heat-transfer direction for further study. It therefore supplies a detailed comparison of definitions rather than a demonstrated common temperature-and-entropy framework.

The supplied review reports that the saved arXiv landing page for the Hecht study lists the related DOI 10.1063/5.0234370. The earlier research identifies a Journal of Chemical Physics article as volume 161, article 224904, dated 9 December 2024, but no retained AIP artifact supports checking that exact publication date or the earlier account of reading its abstract. The scientific findings summarized here derive from the retained preprint described in the review; they should not be read as a separate inspection of the final journal text.

Bebon, Robinson, and Speck's retained manuscript is arXiv:2401.02252v1 from January 2024. It derives dissipation for catalytic active Brownian particles by tracking chemical events through coarse-graining, with ideal chemostats, a small-jump active-Brownian-particle limit, and applications including wall aggregation and motility-induced phase separation. In the model's bookkeeping, dissipated heat is determined by the net number of chemical conversions multiplied by the free energy released per event. This exposes dissipation absent from the reduced equations of motion. More generally, the paper distinguishes trajectory-based entropy production from thermodynamic entropy production: their equality requires inclusion of all degrees of freedom contributing to dissipation.

The saved landing page links the Bebon study to Physical Review X 15, 021050 (2025), DOI 10.1103/PhysRevX.15.021050. It does not establish the earlier stated publication day of 12 May 2025. The supplied review assessed the January 2024 preprint rather than an inspected final journal version, so equivalence of every manuscript detail to the published article is not established. These are model-specific theoretical achievements, not laboratory demonstrations spanning active suspensions and turbulent flows.

The earlier research attributes to Gaspard a New Journal of Physics paper, DOI 10.1088/1367-2630/adf660, dated 1 September 2025, constructing a local Gibbs relation for dilute isothermal suspensions of spherical Janus particles. No retained text is available in the supplied record to verify its identity, date, scope, or result. The attribution remains unresolved; absence of the document does not show that the reported result is false.

Jona-Lasinio's 2023 discussion describes a substantial nonequilibrium framework for diffusive systems that assumes local equilibrium even when the whole system is far from equilibrium. Together, the retained studies establish both existing class-specific progress and reasons to seek better operational connections. They do not demonstrate the proposed common framework, and no direct turbulent-flow thermometry study is supplied. Because the supplied freshness-search record is empty, these materials cannot establish field-wide absence of such a framework as of 1 November 2026.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: apply one operational framework to two different laboratory systems, one active suspension and one externally stirred or turbulent flow. Test a declared range of driving that includes conditions where standard temperature definitions disagree. Three independently calibrated thermometer protocols probing distinct responses should agree within 10 percent, with uncertainty reported. Protocol selection must make the comparison discriminating rather than simply reproduce a subset of definitions already expected to coincide. The 10-percent tolerance is a proposed benchmark, not an established scientific standard.
completion_criteria.label: Three thermometers agree within 10 percent across both systems

completion_criteria.text: Proposed predictive tests: specify the small probe and its coupling, then predict the sign of heat flow into it. Independently measure chemical free-energy input, including conversion rate and free energy per conversion, or the mechanical power supplied by the stirrer. The framework should predict steady dissipation within a factor of two across the declared range. This numerical tolerance is also a proposal. The energy accounting should distinguish heat from mechanical and chemical work and identify which unobserved channels could affect the result.
completion_criteria.label: Heat-flow sign predicted; dissipation accurate within factor of two

completion_criteria.text: Proposed entropy and work tests: define an operational entropy balance, relate its production term to independently measured dissipation under the stated conditions, and test a bound on extractable work using specified reservoirs and an explicit extraction protocol. Temperature agreement alone would not satisfy these requirements. Measurements should also establish whether the proposed entropy behaves as a reproducible state description within the claimed domain or depends on additional variables and preparation history.
completion_criteria.label: Operational entropy balance and extractable-work bounds pass experimental tests

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and boundaries: make calibration procedures, raw measurements, uncertainty estimates, and analysis available for independent reproduction. Repeat the tests with independently prepared systems and varied probe couplings, and report where predictions cease to hold as driving or observation scales change. Success would establish demonstrated breadth across the tested classes and ranges, not literal universality. A result confined to one model or one nondiscriminating regime would not complete this concept.
completion_criteria.label: Reproducible measurements establish prediction limits across driving and observation scales

related_concepts.text: Roster-based comparison: THR-01, A computable thermodynamic potential for far-from-equilibrium continuum transport, is the closest conceptual neighbor. A continuum potential could constrain transport and state changes, while THR-11 asks how temperature and entropy are measured and connected to heat, dissipation, and work. The two could inform one another, but a computable potential and an operational measurement framework are distinct achievements. Only the roster title is supplied for THR-01, so a more specific dependency cannot be established.

Roster-based comparison: THR-07, Synthetic chemomechanical engines whose efficiency approaches biological molecular motors, overlaps through chemical free-energy input, dissipation, and useful work. THR-12, Predictive thermodynamic design of far-from-equilibrium chemical reaction networks, overlaps through fuel-driven dynamics and entropy accounting. THR-09, A thermodynamic design theory of self-replicators, confirmed by a predicted non-biological replicator, could likewise benefit from reliable energetic accounting. THR-11 would supply measurement and accounting capabilities within validated domains; it would not by itself deliver efficient molecular engines, predictive network design, or a functioning predicted replicator. These comparisons follow from the supplied titles rather than full entry descriptions.

Roster-based comparison: THR-02, Useful heat engines that are simultaneously efficient, powerful, and steady, shares the concern with heat-to-work conversion. THR-04, Bulk electronic heat–charge decoupling sufficient for engine-class solid-state conversion, THR-05, A size-extensive quantum advantage in thermodynamic performance, and THR-06, A single-absorber solar converter that uses non-thermal carriers to pass the detailed-balance limit, target particular conversion mechanisms or performance advantages. THR-11 instead targets operational state descriptions and predictive accounting. Better thermometry would not establish heat–charge decoupling, quantum advantage, or a solar-conversion limit breakthrough.

Roster-based comparison: THR-03, General-purpose digital computation near the Landauer scale, and THR-08, Equilibrium sampling computers operating near thermal energy per sample, concern computation under tight thermodynamic energy budgets. Their overlap with THR-11 is the need for meaningful temperature and dissipation measurements. Their completion would require computational functionality and energy performance beyond such measurements; equilibrium sampling also concerns a different operating regime from the strongly driven systems emphasized here.

Roster-based comparison: THR-10, A laboratory measurement of the Unruh temperature, also makes temperature an experimental question, but concerns a specific acceleration-related prediction. THR-11 concerns measurement consistency and entropy accounting in driven material systems. Demonstrating either would not establish the other. These entries remain separate, as do all the other supplied roster concepts.

change_log.change: Replaced the categorical assertion that active and driven systems lack local-equilibrium cells with a conditional statement about relaxation, scale separation, and operational disagreement.
change_log.reason: The supplied review describes far-from-equilibrium diffusive systems that assume local equilibrium and active-matter theories using that assumption. Driving alone does not establish its failure.

change_log.change: Preserved the operational temperature-and-entropy innovation while defining its intended domain explicitly.
change_log.reason: The supported difficulties motivate the concept, but neither the evidence nor a finite experimental program establishes applicability to every driven system.

change_log.change: Integrated approximate agreement within two groups of temperature definitions and the unresolved heat-transfer interpretation.
change_log.reason: The Hecht manuscript contains both findings; thermometer disagreement alone omits useful scientific distinctions and makes an agreement-only completion test too weak.

change_log.change: Expanded hidden-dissipation accounting to include chemical conversions, free energy per event, coarse-graining, and the distinction between trajectory and thermodynamic entropy production.
change_log.reason: These details explain why observed motion and fuel quantity alone can be insufficient and preserve the mechanism described in the reviewed Bebon manuscript.

change_log.change: Separated retained preprint findings from journal metadata and qualified exact publication dates and version equivalence.
change_log.reason: The review establishes the inspected manuscript versions and landing-page links, but not the claimed journal publication days or complete equivalence to final articles.

change_log.change: Corrected the missing-DOI account for the Hecht study and retained the Gaspard attribution with explicit uncertainty.
change_log.reason: The saved arXiv record supplies Hecht's related DOI. No retained AIP or Gaspard text supports the earlier retrieval description or verifies the Gaspard result.

change_log.change: Reframed significance as a conditional extension of existing nonequilibrium thermodynamics and removed the factual generalization about turbulent thermometer disagreement.
change_log.reason: The evidence directly addresses active-particle models and class-specific theory, with no supplied turbulent-flow thermometry study. Existing achievements should not be erased.

change_log.change: Added entropy-balance validation, work-bound tests, independent calibration, discriminating driving conditions, and reproducibility requirements to the proposed completion criteria.
change_log.reason: The original temperature and dissipation tests did not fully test the entropy objective or the claimed ability to constrain extractable work.

change_log.change: Preserved the 10-percent and factor-of-two thresholds as proposed benchmarks and made the limits of finite demonstrations explicit.
change_log.reason: The numbers are author-selected criteria rather than established standards, and success would demonstrate validity only over tested systems and conditions.

change_log.change: Explained relationships to every other supplied roster entry without asserting unverified dependencies on THR-01, THR-07, or THR-12.
change_log.reason: The roster provides titles but not full descriptions. Title-based comparisons support distinctions, not detailed dependency claims.

unresolved_issues: Whether a single temperature-and-entropy pair can adequately describe the intended driven-system classes, or whether additional variables and coupling-dependent descriptions are necessary, remains unresolved.
No supplied evidence demonstrates the proposed framework in turbulent or externally stirred flows, and no direct turbulent-flow thermometry study is included.
The empty freshness-search record prevents a field-wide assessment of whether the target capability remains unachieved as of 1 November 2026.
The Gaspard paper's identity, publication date, local Gibbs relation, and exact applicability remain unverified because no retained text was supplied.
The exact journal publication dates asserted for the Hecht and Bebon studies, the earlier AIP retrieval description, and equivalence of retained preprints to final articles remain unverified.

The numerical benchmarks require justification against achievable uncertainty and useful predictive performance; probe couplings, entropy measurements, reservoirs, and extraction protocols still require concrete experimental specification.
Detailed overlaps and dependencies among roster entries cannot be resolved from titles alone.
